samples.summary: Design doc Phase 25 still documents the removed warn-and-skip credential behaviour of `spec-to-pr.mjs review`, contradicting this change
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:2403-2406 reads: "**Local review is a convenience, not authority:** `spec-to-pr.mjs review` runs the same lenses over the working diff, but needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent. The authoritative panel is still the cloud one". This change deletes exactly that early return (spec-to-pr.mjs `cmdReview`, now `ambientAuthNotice`) and reframes the local run as the only machine review an ordinary branch gets (docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md §1.1, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, .claude/commands/self-review.md). The branch updated agentic-dev-loop.md but left the harness-engineering.md statement of the same subsystem, so the repo now carries two top-level design docs asserting opposite behaviour on the credential question — and the stale one tells a developer the round will silently skip when it will in fact run and bill their logged-in session.

samples.summary: `roundBoundNotice`'s docblock states the bound is "Deliberately NOT a refusal", but the call site refuses without `--force`
samples.evidence: The docblock at spec-to-pr.mjs:216-224 says "Deliberately NOT a refusal … a hard stop would also block the legitimate case … So it says the thing a refusal would be trying to say, and lets the human decide." The call site at :886-888 does `if (notice && !args.force) return fail(notice);`, and MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS at :151 is annotated "ENFORCED — `--force` is the override." Two contradictory statements of the same contract inside one file; the docblock describes a design that was superseded mid-branch and will mislead the next reader about whether the bound gates.

samples.summary: `/self-review` tells the agent `--fresh` is the flag for a reworked branch; the implementation says `--force` is, and `--fresh` is the wrong tool
samples.evidence: self-review.md step 1 says "`--fresh` discards this branch's rounds and starts over after a rework", while the same document's loop section attributes the reworked-branch case to `--force`. spec-to-pr.mjs:880-885 states it explicitly: "`--force` is the override, because the legitimate case exists (a branch reworked enough to deserve a fresh read) and `--fresh` is not it — that discards the carry-forward, which is the opposite of what a fourth round needs." The command file is the only spec an agent reads, so the guidance it gives points at the flag that throws away the carry-forward.

samples.summary: `printable` is a third private copy of the repo's "flatten untrusted text for a human reader" rule, and it diverges from the existing one
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/report-prior.mjs:55-69 already implements this semantic (`plain`), and its own comment insists on "one semantic for 'untrusted text a stranger wrote that a person will read', not two" (mirroring notification.service.ts). `printable` (spec-to-pr.mjs:286-293) re-implements the C0/C1 → space + whitespace-collapse half in the same directory but omits `plain`'s zero-width / bidi-override strip (`[​-‏‪-‮…]`), which is the part that matters most for a terminal surface a developer reads to decide whether the branch is clean. Neither copy is extracted into a shared module, so the two answers to the same question will keep diverging.

samples.summary: The task file's Verification section records behaviour the branch no longer has (`--round 4` "still runs")
samples.evidence: Line 85-86: "`--round 4` prints the bound advisory and still runs". The shipped command refuses round 4 unless `--force` (spec-to-pr.mjs:886-888), and self-review.md documents the refusal. The evidence recorded for the change describes a superseded revision.

samples.summary: The todo diagnosed the module's name as the reason the capability reads as agent-track-only, and the fix is a header comment plus a slash command rather than extraction
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260917-self-review-loop-todo.md:66-68: "The review lives inside `spec-to-pr.mjs`, whose name says 'agent track'. That is the whole reason the capability reads as unavailable to hand-driven work." The change instead adds a ~7-line disclaimer at spec-to-pr.mjs:20-26 and ~500 lines of self-review-specific round bookkeeping into the handoff module, leaving a single file that owns two unrelated front doors. A `self-review.mjs` (importing the shared helpers) would put the loop at the layer its own docs place it. No behavioural consequence; noting it as a layering preference.

samples.summary: "all six lenses" vs the design doc's "all seven lens checks" for the same panel
samples.evidence: self-review.md says "The panel itself always runs all six lenses"; docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md §1.1 (and the todo) say #1061 "got all seven" lens checks. scripts/agent/lenses/ holds six lens markdown files, so one of the two counts is describing check runs rather than lenses. Worth stating consistently in the two docs a reader will compare.
